title: Consolidated cut-signal taxonomy and GTM handshake plan for API/Console/Runtime
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: produce a single operational taxonomy of 'cut signals' and a lightweight GTM handshake playbook that the API, Console, and Runtime teams can use during the release train. Deliverables: (1) Cut-signal taxonomy (hard vs soft signals, owner, threshold, verification steps), (2) Per-lane gating matrix mapping signals to scope-lock decisions, (3) GTM handshake checklist (who calls the cut, comm channels, templated release notes snippets), (4) Last-mile runbook for unblocking / emergency scope fallbacks. Rationale: many recent launches relied on ad-hoc decisions; consolidating signals reduces release friction, makes cut criteria auditable, and speeds go/no-go decisions across teams.
acceptance_criteria: A documented taxonomy with at least 12 discrete signals classified as hard or soft
A gating matrix that covers API, Console, and Runtime with clear owners for each signal
A GTM handshake checklist with assigned comm channels and templated release-note snippets
A validated last-mile runbook exercised in a tabletop scenario with at least two cross-functional stakeholders
Sign-off from Eng, DX (developer experience), and GTM leads recorded in the Confluence page
notes: Trade-offs: keep taxonomy lightweight to avoid policing edge cases; prefer actionable signals (latency SLO breach, critical blocker, regression in smoke tests) over vague metrics
Decision: use 'hard' signals to force scope lock and automatic rollback; 'soft' signals should trigger mitigation plans but not block release by default
Suggestion: integrate a short Slack / PagerDuty channel naming convention (e.g., #release-gtm-<train>) and a single Google Doc for release notes to avoid edit conflicts
Scope: excludes downstream marketplace partners (handled by separate partner-runbooks) but includes affected telemetry and billing changes
